memory_scope.sampling: Phase boundaries only, outside CPU windows; not a sampled memory-peak test.
memory_scope.processes: All observed Guard cgroup processes and descendant cgroups; membership and /proc reads are not atomic. Vanished or replaced processes remain unknown, not zero.
memory_scope.rss: RSS sums can count shared pages more than once. PSS divides mapped shared pages among processes.
memory_scope.cgroup: memory.current/peak include charged memory beyond process mappings; memory.peak is the cgroup lifetime peak, not this phase alone. memory.stat contains overlapping categories.
memory_scope.tmpfs: statvfs allocated usage and capacity for /run/rescue and /run; contents are shared by Guard, rescue shell, agent and sampler. This is not Guard-exclusive memory.
memory_scope.overlap: Do not add process PSS, cgroup usage and tmpfs usage: mapped/charged pages overlap. No unprotected baseline was measured, so total incremental protection cost is unknown.
memory_scope.swapping: tmpfs noswap protects file pages, not Python anonymous heap or stacks. Guard memory.swap.max=0 separately prevents anonymous swapping for the group and descendants; memory.max=128MiB caps charged memory. Neither is mlock or a pressure-survival guarantee, and not all tmpfs pages preloaded by other cgroups are charged here.
memory_scope.limits: No memory-pressure, OOM, long disconnection, full fault-domain budget or independent rescue scheduling validation in this healthy run.

limitations: All pass flags refer to the selected test contract; expected failures are not application recoveries.
A pending lower I/O can retain one D-state worker and flock indefinitely; the experiment explicitly releases it.
The five randomized SIGKILL samples all landed in verifying; fixed hooks cover other userspace-visible phases.
No claim of arbitrary in-kernel schedule coverage, physical USB power-loss durability, or host production readiness.
Failure-contract runs have no offline acknowledged-data audit.
Functional baseline and faulted Git runs overlapped on the host; their latency numbers are not isolated performance comparisons.
Resource PSS, cgroup and tmpfs views overlap and are not summed; a full unprotected-memory baseline is not provided.
